title: Panels Atelier prototype + accessibility report for cost operator lenses
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: The cost explorer and rollout inspector surfaces are increasingly populated with small, dense cards and interactive panels. Teams have asked for a lightweight, reusable panel component set that supports compact telemetry, multiple rollout states, and clear cost signal hierarchy while meeting AA/AAA accessibility targets for contrast and motion-reduce.

Scope: Prototype a ‘Panels Atelier’ — a family of components (compact card, expandable rail, state badges, micro-sparklines) and a token map (spacing, elevation, color ramps, interactive focus) that integrates into the Console design system and the cost operator lens patterns. Deliverables: Figma prototype, accessibility contrast report, component guidelines doc, and a small set of developer-ready tokens for runtime feature flags.

Goals:
- Create a single, adaptable panel component that covers three density modes (compact, regular, expanded).
- Ensure text/icon contrast >= 4.5:1 for body and >= 3:1 for secondary UI where appropriate; produce remediation patterns for low-contrast legacy variants.
- Define a rollout-state system (healthy / degraded / fallback / canary) with semantic color tokens and motion prescriptions for transitions.
- Produce a token export (name, hex/rgba, elevation) for the frontend team and a Figma components library page for Console.

Out of scope: full migration of existing console cards (will be follow-up by infra and product roadmaps).

Why this matters: Cost surfaces are mission-critical for customers using Redwood Dedicated and Hosted; inconsistent panels lead to misread signals and support churn. A standardized Atelier will reduce design debt and speed feature rollouts across teams.
acceptance_criteria: Figma file 'Panels Atelier' contains variants for compact/regular/expanded panels and a token page
Contrast report shows remediation or alternate styles for any token failing 4.5:1 for primary body text
Rollout-state visual system (4 states) documented with tokens and accessible labels
Developer token export provided (CSS custom properties and JSON palette) with names matching Console token taxonomy
Sign-off from Accessibility and Console Product PMs
Prototype validated in a short usability run (>=5 engineers/product reviewers) with feedback captured
comments: 2026-03-02 — Maya Chen: Initial exploration sketches complete; prototype will reuse the new metric-chip tokens introduced last cycle. Raised question about whether canary state should animate or be static for reduced-motion users.
2026-03-04 — Diego Alvarez: Merged initial component frames into Figma and started token map. Marked a11y as required. Planned a short contrast sweep with the accessibility team next week.

2026-03-06 — Priya Nambiar (Accessibility): Ran automated contrast checks; three token pairs fail 4.5:1 for body. Proposed two options: increase weight/size for body text in compact mode OR introduce a semantic strong token for cost values. Recommend a design decision call.

2026-03-08 — Evan Park (Frontend): Reviewed Figma export; asked for semantic token names (e.g., --console-panel-bg-01) and a matching elevation token for shadow parity on VPC console. Also noted micro-sparkline color needs alpha backdrop to pass low-vision tests.

2026-03-10 — Maya Chen: Held design sync with PM and Frontend; agreed to add 'strong-text' semantic token and to raise compact body size by 1px only in compact variant to preserve density. Documented trade-off: slight density loss vs. accessibility compliance.
2026-03-11 — Diego Alvarez: Prototype iteration pushed. Accessibility remediation applied; waiting on PM sign-off for rollout-state copy and ARIA roles.

2026-03-12 — Lena Fong (Product): Reviewed prototype; requested clearer affordance for panel expand/collapse in keyboard-only flows and asked to include test scenarios for rollouts that show automatic fallback state transitions.
decisions: Adopt semantic token '--panel-strong-text' to address contrast failures instead of increasing heavy-handed typography changes across console
Canary state will use a subtle 120ms cross-fade for color changes; motion-reduce preference will serve an immediate color swap with no opacity animation
Compact variant will bump body size from 12px to 13px for body text only; labels and micro copy remain 11px to preserve density
Micro-sparklines will use an 80% opacity overlay against panel-bg tokens to increase perceived contrast without changing the palette
